title: Centres and Peripheries in Gender History: A Historiographical Review
locator: Indexed publisher abstract; direct page returned 403
statement: Dialeti examines regional historiographies and journal coverage to question how academic centres and peripheries shape gender history.

title: A Companion to Global Gender History, second edition
statement: The updated companion organizes gender history across regions, periods and themes, providing a survey framework beyond a small canon of individual theorists.
date_note: Online 2020 and copyright 2021 retained; do not interpret as distinct works.

title: State of the Field: Disability History
statement: Blackie and Moncrieff connect disability history to activism, sociocultural interpretation and the recovery of experience from mediated sources.

title: The Oxford Handbook of Disability History
statement: The handbook broadens disability history across periods and regions, giving a route to test coverage beyond modern Anglo-American rights movements.

title: On Borderlands
statement: Hämäläinen and Truett foreground mobility, contingent identities and contested power at imperial and national margins; this extract concerns North America.

title: Geographies of Knowing, Geographies of Ignorance: Jumping Scale in Southeast Asia
statement: Van Schendel questions area-studies boundaries and proposes alternative spatial configurations, including borderlands and transnational flows.

title: State of the Field: Digital History
locator: Opening chronology and Quantitative Text Analysis, extracted lines 326–334
statement: Romein and colleagues distinguish successive computing practices and stress that corpus composition and changing meanings constrain quantitative text analysis.

title: The Transformation of Historical Research in the Digital Age
statement: Milligan treats search, digitization and online scholarly practice as changes affecting ordinary historical research, not only specialist computational projects.

title: The Archived Web: Doing History in the Digital Age
statement: Brügger treats the archived web as both historical evidence and an object of historical inquiry, requiring its own source criticism.

title: History in the Age of Abundance? How the Web Is Transforming Historical Research
statement: Milligan develops research questions around large web archives and the problems created by abundant born-digital evidence.

title: The History of Emotions: An Interview with William Reddy, Barbara Rosenwein, and Peter Stearns
statement: The interview contrasts emotional regimes, communities and emotionology, and presents emotion as a category usable across historical fields.

title: Are Emotions a Kind of Practice (and Is That What Makes Them Have a History)? A Bourdieuan Approach to Understanding Emotion
statement: Scheer proposes understanding emotions through embodied practice, making the body and learned activity part of historical explanation.

title: A Sensory History Manifesto
statement: Smith argues that sensory history should become a general historical habit while retaining critical debate about historically formed sensory experience.

title: Taste and the History of Science: Introduction
statement: Hendriksen and Wragge-Morley challenge the exclusion of taste from histories of scientific knowledge and connect sensory practice with knowledge production.

title: The History of Knowledge
locator: Opening overview, contents and programme; prior pilot selected circulation passages
statement: Östling and Heidenblad organize inquiry around knowledge actors, forms and circulation; boundaries with neighbouring histories remain a research question.
date_note: Online 2023; print 2024 already distinguished in the prior pilot.

title: The History of Science and the History of Knowledge
locator: Previously checked pilot hk_01–hk_02; exact evidence joins retained in legacy-bridge.json
statement: Daston opens inquiry beyond established science while questioning what gives the expanded history of knowledge coherence.

title: What Is Trans History? From Activist and Academic Roots, a Field Takes Shape
locator: Feature body, field formation and historian interviews
statement: Agarwal documents exchanges between activist and academic history and disputes over terminology and the recovery of lives before modern identity labels.

title: What Is Trans History, Anyway? Historiographical Theory and Practice in a Flourishing Field

statement: Hickman proposes a three-part account of trans historiography and identifies competing temporal starting points; these are her categories, not a settled taxonomy.

title: State of the Field: The Modern History of Childhood

statement: Tisdall questions universal developmental assumptions and examines childhood in relation to adulthood, power and the interpretation of children’s evidence.

statement: The article proposes closer work between childhood and education histories through transnational comparison, socialization and children’s school-produced sources.
